analysis:
Only this doc changed: docs/operations/provider-release.md. It describes a release-pipeline change whose workflow and scripts are not in this batch: .github/workflows/release-dev-branch.yml, release-swift.yml, release-provider.yml, scripts/provider_release_resume/api.py verify_workflow_source, scripts/resolve-provider-release.sh and scripts/install.sh.

Changed behavior:
- Master pushes no longer publish dev releases.
- The dev-branch lane changes from a master-dispatched, ad-hoc-signed and secret-free build to a push-triggered build on `dev`, signed with Developer ID and inheriting all repository secrets (head 503-535).
- The master gate admits a `dev` push for env `dev` only (head 293-301).
- The doc states that dev builds meet the production self-updater requirement (head 303-309).
- Review is not enforced on `dev` (head 542-546).

The base text claimed that branch code never held a secret or the production signing identity (base 479-507). That claim is removed, which is a new supply-chain surface for T-013/T-054 and the A-005/A-011/A-017 secrets and identity registries.

Production App Attest still requires durable qualification on the prod coordinator. That should keep dev builds out of prod serving, but this is not verified here. Legacy APNs code-identity on a shared bundle ID (base 406-413) may let a Developer-ID dev build answer production challenges; T-042 interaction is unverified.

For integration, check:
- Whether release-dev-branch.yml references the reusable workflow locally (editable by a dev push) or pinned to master.
- Whether `secrets: inherit` exposes PROD_* and Apple secrets to jobs that run dev-controlled steps.
- Whether `dev` branch protection exists.
- The ReleaseVersionGreater ranking (head 549-570). It is an availability and ordering note only; publish-release may fail.

findings.detail:
The new runbook (head 503-546) makes every push to the `dev` branch start `release-dev-branch.yml`. That workflow calls the reusable `release-provider.yml` with `secrets: inherit` and no GitHub environment (head 528: "All of these are repository secrets"). The build is signed with the production Developer ID. It meets the production self-updater requirement (Apple anchor, `io.darkbloom.provider`, `SLDQ2GJ6TL`) and shares the production keychain access group. The doc admits that review is not enforced on `dev` (head 542-546). The base lane was dispatch-only on master, ad-hoc signed, and ran branch code without secrets.

Trigger: anyone who can push to `dev` changes provider code, or changes the workflow YAML that runs for that push. That YAML includes the reusable workflow if it is referenced locally. The `environment == 'prod'` guards (head 531-535) live in YAML that a dev push can edit, so they do not protect secrets. Only master's source gate script is fixed.

Impact:
- Exfiltration of `PROD_RELEASE_KEY`, `PROD_R2_*` and the Apple signing and notarization credentials.
- Unreviewed code shipped under the production team signature. It could read co-installed production keychain items, such as provider tokens.
- The binary-identity assumptions in T-013 and T-054 no longer hold.

Fix: before enabling the lane, require PR review on `dev`, or keep `dev` unsigned or ad-hoc signed. Put prod and Apple secrets behind protected GitHub environments scoped to master or tags. Pass secrets explicitly instead of `secrets: inherit`. Pin the reusable workflow to master's reviewed copy.
findings.title: Unreviewed `dev` pushes would get Developer ID signing and inherited production secrets
